position.summary: According to the text, in the week of approximately October 8 through 14, 2026, several major storylines converged on Switzerland. Guy Parmelin announced his resignation from the Federal Council effective year-end, just after a high-profile visit to India where he signed memoranda of understanding with Prime Minister Modi on mobility, transport, science, and innovation. UBS faced sustained investor pressure over Swiss capital rules, with CEO Sergio Ermotti arguing the bank needs a US presence to compete globally. The Swiss franc rallied amid French budget worries, European bond stress, and weak US jobs data. The Court of Arbitration for Sport in Lausanne prepared to rule on the Senegal-Morocco Africa Cup of Nations title appeal. UEFA leaders met in Berlin to organize a challenge to FIFA president Gianni Infantino, while Norway filed ethics complaints against him. The organizing president of the Crans-Montana Alpine World Championships was suspended pending a fraud trial. Swiss glaciers had lost nearly 20 percent of their mass in five years, and Lake Constance ferries were suspended due to low water. The UN Human Rights Council in Geneva adopted a resolution demanding an immediate ceasefire in Sudan. Julius Baer executed a share buyback, Partners Group restructured its flagship fund, and billionaires relocated from the UK toward Switzerland, Monaco, and the UAE. The Swiss national team beat Slovenia 2-1 in the Nations League.
